open_points.subject: A18 backup snapshot concurrency
open_points.text: “a change committed while the copy is made goes on, is not in this backup and is in the next”
open_points.question: Does “is in the next” guarantee that every intervening committed change remains represented in the next backup, or only that the next backup snapshots whatever state still exists when its read transaction begins?
options: Every intervening commit must remain represented in the next backup, even if later operations remove its effects
The next backup contains only the state visible at its own snapshot instant, so an intervening commit may leave no representation
The guarantee applies only when the committed change has not subsequently been reversed or erased
open_points.default_guess: Treat each backup as an independent current-state snapshot; the next backup contains the change only if its effects or an unerased audit entry still exist then.

witness.initial: A daily backup's read transaction is copying an active project.
events: Cabinet Kernel adds a room while the copy is in progress; the transaction commits, and room creation writes no audit entry.
The owner archives the project and then anonymises it before the next daily backup; anonymisation removes all rooms.
The next daily backup takes its snapshot.
outcomes: Under the literal “is in the next” guarantee, the next backup must somehow represent the committed room addition.
Under the snapshot model stated elsewhere, the next backup contains the anonymised project and no room or audit entry representing that addition.
witness.observer: The owner restoring or inspecting the next backup
